question: May a G1 row land when its scaffolding helper's implicit copy-constructor COMDAT ??0<C>@@QAE@ABV0@@Z (unreferenced, NOADDR: retail has no out-of-line copy, Clone inlines it) is (a) byte-and-reloc identical to a landed copy that comes from a row-local model, not the shared header (47 rows), or (b) different from the landed pick-any copy / new to the build (9 rows)?
evidence: batches/g1_r1 (56 rows, every one: vland RELOCATION_MATCH PASS HEAD and new, strict leaf + relabelled catalog name with 0 WARN, leaf bytes equal to HEAD, vtcheck VT_EQ v the retail vftable, pk 0 NEQ / 0 reach flips, census /FORCE link 0 new duplicates / 0 new unresolved; CHECKS.tsv). VC7.1 emits the implicit copy ctor whenever the helper uses it, and every helper form measured emits it (placement new, a local copy, a derived probe class: exp/scaf, work/cc_scaf*.log); the class's VIRTUAL_MODEL header declares no constructor, so the copy ctor is the only vtable emitter. Landed precedent: 0x009539C0 / 0x008CA9A0 (NF255) and the 7 ACCEPT rows' landed Clone rows emit the same COMDAT. Nothing references it once /OPT:REF drops the helper.
proposal: Accept (a) as R10 tier 1 widened to an identical landed copy from any model (same bytes, same relocations), and (b) as scaffolding like the helper itself, queuing the differing landed copy's row as R10 debt. If refused, these rows wait for a ctor declaration opt-in in each VIRTUAL_MODEL header.
